item.text:
**1B.8 Research Note: Ali Khamenei in 2024**

**Bottom line:** the 2024 record shows **some tactical de-escalation and channel-preserving behavior**, but not a consistently clear or reassuring crisis-management posture. The strongest positive evidence is Iran’s muted response to the April 19 Isfahan incident and continued IAEA talks later in the year. The strongest negative evidence is Khamenei’s own celebratory rhetoric after the April 13 strike on Israel and his October call for allies to intensify the struggle.

| Title | Publisher | Date | Recoverable URL | Claim-level summary | Question IDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|
| `Tehran signals no retaliation against Israel after drones attack Iran` | Reuters | 2024-04-19 | [link](https://www.theprint.in/world/tehran-signals-no-retaliation-against-israel-after-drones-attack/2048236/) | Tehran played down the reported strike near Isfahan and indicated it had no retaliation plan; Reuters said this response appeared aimed at averting region-wide war. This is the clearest 2024 de-escalation signal tied to Khamenei’s system. | `1B.8`, `1B.1` |
| `IAEA's Grossi seeks deal with Iran on nuclear steps 'soon'` | Reuters | 2024-05-07 | [link](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/iaeas-grossi-seeks-deal-with-iran-on-nuclear-steps-soon-3425312) | After visiting Iran, the IAEA chief said talks would continue and a package of measures should be reached soon. This supports that Iran kept a verification channel open during a crisis year, which helps reduce accidental escalation. | `1B.8`, `1B.4`, `1B.7` |
| `Iran will not impede IAEA access, head of its atomic organisation says` | Reuters | 2024-12-14 | [link](https://theprint.in/world/iran-will-not-impede-iaea-access-head-of-its-atomic-organisation-says/2403254/) | Iran’s atomic chief said the country would not obstruct UN nuclear-watchdog access and would work within safeguards. Late-year this suggests the channel for technical communication was still being maintained rather than shut down. | `1B.8`, `1B.4`, `1B.7` |
| `Supreme Leader Khamenei says Iran demonstrated its power against Israel` | Reuters | 2024-04-21 | [link](https://www.theprint.in/world/supreme-leader-khamenei-says-iran-demonstrated-its-power-against-israel/2050451/) | Khamenei thanked the armed forces for the April strike on Israel, described it as proof of Iran’s power, and urged continued military innovation. That is not de-escalatory crisis communication; it signals pride in escalation and keeps pressure on the adversary. | `1B.8`, `1B.1` |
| `Iran’s Khamenei urges allies to step up struggle against Israel` | Reuters | 2024-10-05 | [link](https://www.theprint.in/world/irans-khamenei-urges-allies-to-step-up-struggle-against-israel/2298142/) | In his first Friday prayer sermon in nearly five years, Khamenei called for more anti-Israel struggle and urged regional allies to “double your efforts and capabilities.” That is a direct signal against crisis de-escalation and a broader-war risk. | `1B.8`, `1B.1`, `1B.6` |

**Assessment**

- **Positive side:** Khamenei’s system sometimes chose muted or technically bounded responses, and Iran kept the IAEA channel open.
- **Negative side:** his own public rhetoric in crisis moments was still confrontational and triumphalist, not consistently calming or clarity-enhancing.
- **Net reading for 2024:** **partial and tactical de-escalation, but not robust crisis discipline**.

**Search gap**

- I did **not** find a strong 2024 primary-source example of Khamenei explicitly using a crisis hotline, public backchannel, or structured communication protocol to reduce accidental war.
- I also did **not** find a clear direct statement from Khamenei personally framing April 19 as a de-escalation choice; that inference comes from Reuters’ description of Tehran’s muted response and the preservation of diplomatic channels.
